newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wool outlook remains optimistic.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wool outlook remains optimistic.

text.p: Australian wool prices are expected to continue their gradual upward trend this week, according to the Australian Council of Wool Exporters (ACWE) and pastoral group Wesfarmers Dalgety Ltd.
The ACWE said exporters expect demand for wool to increase as Europeans return from summer holidays and supply increases over the next few weeks.
Wesfarmers said this week's smaller offering of 69,468 bales in Sydney and Fremantle would again have a positive effect.

To counteract this, there will not be the same amount of finer, good quality types available (considering the large Fremantle selection of broader wools) reducing the upward pressure on prices, Wesfarmers said. Price differentials for individual microns are therefore expected to continue widening.

"Fine wool price strength is further anticipated owing to Japanese, Korean and European demand for the limited supply of good quality types," Wesfarmers said. "Prices for broader wools are expected to remain stagnant with weakening tendencies, suffering from a lack of Chinese activity in the auction room, necessary to boost this end of the market," Wesfarmers said.
